0.content: Ningguang's palace floats above Liyue Harbor on plaustrite, a levitating stone she bought in astronomical quantities. It began as a single room and grew until it blots out the moon over Liyue. Only she and three trusted confidants may enter its working rooms. There they pin up summaries of intelligence while she looks out over the city, decides, then shreds everything and throws it out of the window. The falling "paper snow" warns merchants that a change is coming. Save for Mora, it is what she loves most, "because it is infinite", and she means its shadow to reach all seven nations.

1.content: The Crux's captain flouts Liyue's rules, smuggling exotic goods and claiming to enact justice and keep sailors employed. Ningguang has fined her heavily so often that "the fines she has paid would be enough to buy her a whole new ship". She tried to persuade her privately, gave up, and now asks the Traveler to keep Beidou out of her sight. Yet rumour says Ningguang secretly runs The Crux. Both deny it: Ningguang because she picked Beidou personally, not The Crux, to do her dirty work; Beidou because she works with Ningguang as an equal. Ningguang's verdict: "Beidou is the most reliable person in Liyue." Tell her the truth and what's in it for her, and she will come round.

2.content: The Yuheng once thought Ningguang treated Liyue as nothing but a marketplace, with profit as her only principle. Ningguang thought Keqing too hard-headed and cleaned up after her behind the scenes. When Keqing declared that the time of the adepti had passed and the Qixing must face it, Ningguang's doubts were "dispelled". After Rex Lapis's departure Keqing calls her a comrade in arms, though they still disagree often. When asked whether Liyue is better off with the new Keqing or the old, Ningguang says only time will tell.

3.content: Yelan claims to work for the Ministry of Civil Affairs, but she is Ningguang's intelligence agent for national security. They met long before Ningguang was a Qixing and worked together; Yelan jokes she may be partly why Ningguang rose so quickly. Ningguang recommended the job and calls Yelan someone she trusts "unreservedly". In public Yelan calls her "Lady". Yelan's network has kept foreign intelligence rings out of Liyue.

4.content: Ningguang presided over the 1.1 Rite of Descension; when Rex Lapis's body fell onto the offering table she ordered the exits sealed. She hid the Exuvia and imposed a gag order to keep control and prevent another crisis like Mondstadt's, while letting the Rite of Parting proceed. She denies the Qixing killed their god but admits his passing seems advantageous to them. At the Rite of Parting she told the adepti that Rex Lapis had appeared to her in a dream, and she had dared not speak to him.

5.content: When Tartaglia freed Osial to force Rex Lapis out, Ningguang united the Qixing with the adepti: "we have agreed to put our differences aside for now." The Jade Chamber's formation powered the Guizhong Ballistae with adeptal energy while Fatui troops attacked; she promised Snezhnaya's diplomats would answer "every last one". When the ballistae fell, she asked the Traveler for help and drove the Jade Chamber into the sea onto the wounded god.

6.comment: Ningguang: Beisht and the new Jade Chamber
6.content: In 2.4 Ningguang publicly offered generous pay and one honest answer to the first three people who brought her the rarest materials for a new Jade Chamber. The winners were the Traveler (with Shenhe, who brought the Adepti Sigils), Yun Jin and Beidou. She gave Yun Jin the Chamber as her opera venue and told the Traveler she did not know where the sibling was. When the Chamber rose, Osial's wife Beisht attacked as expected: Ningguang had chosen to rebuild then to draw her out. She declared that in this human age Liyue must overcome the crisis on its own strength, and the Chamber, Keqing's ballistae and Beidou's fleet struck together.

7.comment: Ningguang: Secretaries, informants and the paper snow
7.content: Only three trusted confidants may enter the Jade Chamber's working areas; her secretaries Baiwen, Baishi and Baixiao work there. The children of Liyue Harbor are her real "eyes and ears": they report every meeting and newcomer in exchange for treats, and she cross-checks their reports. The rumour that she eavesdrops through enchanted walls is false.

8.comment: Ningguang: The Tianquan and Liyue's laws
8.content: The Qixing are seven equal leaders named after the Big Dipper's stars; the Tianquan keeps the book of ancient laws set down by Morax and every later amendment, and handles foreign relations. Each Tianquan amends the laws to fit the times; the commentary runs to 279 pages, and every citizen receives a copy. Ningguang likes it so: law and order is good for business, and she knows its intricacies better than anyone. Merchants hunt loopholes; she closes them so fast she is privately nicknamed the "Tailor of Liyue".
